text: Live coding moves quickly. One missing line can leave a beginner stuck while the stream carries on. Copying the instructor's entire project may fix the problem, but it can also erase the learner's own ideas.

Rejoin gives learners a way back without starting over. It brings a private coding workspace, clear lesson checkpoints, and guided recovery alongside a Twitch workshop. The goal is simple: keep learning, and keep your work.

The instructor has a dedicated console. Move the class between three checkpoints, publish a teaching note, or pause the workshop when people need time. Optional community signals show where help is needed, while small public groups stay hidden.

Twitch chat becomes the live remote control. Checkpoint C one, C two, and C three move the lesson. Pause gives everyone breathing room. Rejoin returns the workshop link. Linked learners use stuck and ready to share their status. Every command begins with an exclamation mark.

Learners join without creating an account. Choose a recovery target, personalize the title and styles, and work in the HTML, CSS, and JavaScript editor. Changes save on this device, and the instructor moving ahead never replaces your project.

When something stops working, choose Help me continue. Start with a teaching hint, or ask AI a question. Before AI receives anything, review the exact script and give permission. Your other files stay private.

Rejoin suggests a focused change instead of replacing the project. Review the before and after, check the suggestion, and approve it yourself. Now the RSVP button works, and the event still has your own title and style.
You stay in control. Protect a file to prevent automatic changes. Keep a valid alternative solution. And if you edit after a repair, undo offers a separate earlier copy, preserving your newer work.

Need a person instead? Select the files for a help packet, review the redacted contents, then choose whom to share it with. Export your project, import it later, or download a recovery receipt with your changes and remaining work.

Community sharing is optional and reversible. Share a checkpoint or blocker category without sending your code or private question. The stream overlay shows the lesson and approved group signals. You can unlink Twitch or delete your workspace whenever you choose.

When the live workshop ends, your learning does not have to stop. Continue with local practice, lesson guidance, checks, and exports. Rejoin helps a community move forward together, while every learner keeps a project that is still their own.
